title: Multi-objective particle swarm optimisation
outline: Lecture 15 video (Nature-Inspired Computation, ECM3412): Multi-objective particle swarm optimisation. 9 scenes, 115 s: title (4), no single best (12), pbest rules (15), the archive (16), pruning by crowding (15), leaders (17), a MOPSO run (13), many objectives (14), recap (9). STORY (lessons order). 15.1 (l15-archive, js/content/nic/l15-01.js): PSO follows pbest and gbest; with two objectives (drone routes: time and energy, both minimised) the best is a set: SWARM9 A..I, front A B C E G. pbest rules: keep oldest (replace only if new dominates old) vs keep newest (replace unless old dominates new): from (5,5) moves (4,6) (6,7) (3.5,5.5) (4.5,4) give oldest (5,5) (5,5) (5,5) (4.5,4) and newest (4,6) (4,6) (3.5,5.5) (4.5,4). Archive update: a newcomer removes every member it dominates and joins unless a member dominates it (ARCH a1..a5; (2,4) removes a2 a3 and joins; (5,4.5) is dominated by (2,4) and turned away; (7,2) joins; final 5). 15.2 (l15-bounded, l15-02.js): cap the archive; prune by crowding distance, ends infinity, remove smallest and recompute: P12 a..l to cap 6 removes j 0.13, f 0.17, c 0.19, k 0.34, g 0.46, b 0.50, keeps a d e h i l (clustering not shown). 15.3 (l15-leaders, l15-03.js): leaders from the archive: random (1 in 5), dominated-solution count (H a..e vs SW P..V: counts a1 b1 c4 d2 e1, weight 1/(1+n): c 1/5, e 1/2), hypervolume contribution with the particle as reference (P (7,7.5): b 1.5, c 4, d 1.5, total 12, c leads); many objectives: comparable share 2/2^M (1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/32). Scene 7 is a real run of the lessons drone MOPSO (l15-02.js engine, seed 4, cap 10, crowding prune, random leader, keep newest): archive 5 at iteration 0, 10 at 20. Workshop 15.W (l15-workshop.js drone route MOPSO lab). Not covered: clustering prune, sparse-leader tournament, average rank, distance ranking. ALL NUMBERS computed in videos/l15/common.js by the lessons kernel and asserted at load. COLOURS: green = archive / non-dominated / kept; red = dominated / removed / turned away; blue = the particle, new position, newcomer; purple = keep-oldest rule; orange = keep-newest rule and attention (infinity, crowding values, chosen leader); grey = neutral. LAYOUT: L15.plot (L13.plot preset) at x 12, y 12, 600 x 616 with axes time / energy 0..10, right panel x 636..924; scene 8 uses its own square and bars. Text >= 28 px, symbols as SVG.

titleCard.title: Multi-objective particle swarm optimisation
titleCard.sub: How a swarm keeps a whole front of best trade-offs

title: Two goals, so
no single gbest
caps: Nine drone routes, each scored by time and energy. Lower is better.
Plain PSO follows two points: its own pbest and the swarm's gbest.
Five routes are not dominated by any other route.
None beats the other four, so there is no single gbest.
scenes.spec: Lecture 15 video, scene 02-nobest: lesson 15.1's nine drone routes A..I (L15.SWARM9; time and energy, both minimised). Plain PSO follows two remembered points, pbest and gbest. With two goals, five routes (A B C E G) are non-dominated and none beats the other four, so there is no single gbest to follow. Layout (stage px): L15.plot at x 12, y 12, 600 x 616; right panel x 636..924: card 'pbest' (y 12) and card 'gbest' (y 182). Story (local seconds): 0.3 plot, 0.6 nine grey routes pop in; 3.2 the two cards, F turns blue (the particle); 6.0 the five non-dominated routes turn green and the front line draws; 8.8 orange dashed arrows from F to all five, the gbest card turns orange: 'gbest: ?'; hold to 12.

title: When should
pbest move?
caps: A particle's pbest starts at (5, 5). Lower time and energy are better.
It moves to (4, 6), a trade-off. Keep oldest stays, keep newest moves.
(6, 7) is worse on both goals, so neither rule moves.
(3.5, 5.5) is another trade-off: only keep newest moves.
(4.5, 4) dominates (5, 5), so now keep oldest moves too.
scenes.spec: Lecture 15 video, scene 03-pbest: lesson 15.1's two pbest rules on one particle's four moves from pbest (5, 5) (L15.MOVES, L15.PB). Keep oldest (purple): move only if the new position dominates pbest. Keep newest (orange): move unless pbest dominates the new position. Oldest: (5,5) (5,5) (5,5) (4.5,4); newest: (4,6) (4,6) (3.5,5.5) (4.5,4). Layout (stage px): L15.plot x 12, y 12, 600 x 616, axes 2..8; right panel x 636..924: purple rule card (y 12, h 136), orange rule card (y 160, h 136), then four move rows (y 320 + 76 i): the move's position, a purple and an orange mark (tick = that rule's pbest moves, grey minus = it stays). Story (local seconds): 0.3 plot, 0.6 both pbest markers on (5, 5) (purple big disc, orange small disc on top), 0.8 and 1.1 the rule cards; moves at 3.2 / 6.6 / 9.2 / 12.0: the new position pops in blue with its row, 1.0 s later the marks pop and the markers glide (0.6 s) to their new places; earlier moves stay as small grey dots; hold to 15.

title: Keep every route
nobody beats
caps: The archive keeps every non-dominated route found so far.
Newcomer (2, 4) dominates two members: they leave and it joins.
(5, 4.5) is dominated by (2, 4), so it is turned away.
(7, 2) is a new trade-off: nobody dominates it, so it joins.
No member dominates another: the archive is the front so far.
scenes.spec: Lecture 15 video, scene 04-archive: lesson 15.1's archive update (L15.ARCH a1..a5, L15.NEWS: three newcomers in turn). Each newcomer y gets two boxes: blue (up and right of y: the members y dominates, they leave) and red (down and left of y: a member there dominates y, so y is turned away). (2, 4) removes a2 and a3 and joins; (5, 4.5) is dominated by (2, 4) and is turned away; (7, 2) is a new trade-off and joins. Final archive a1 (2,4) a4 a5 (7,2): five members. Layout (stage px): L15.plot x 12, y 12, 600 x 616; right panel x 636..924: blue legend card (y 12, h 150), red legend card (y 176, h 150), stat 'archive' (y 360) with the member count. Story (local seconds): 0.3 plot, 0.6 five green members, 1.6 legend cards and stat; newcomers at 3.2 / 6.8 / 10.2: +0 y pops in blue, +0.5 both boxes grow, +1.4 crosses on removed members (or on y), +2.0 they fade, +2.2 a joining y turns green, +2.6 boxes fade; 13.4 the green front line draws through the final five; hold to 16.

title: Too many? Drop
the most crowded
caps: Twelve archive members, but the cap is six.
The two ends, a and l, get infinite crowding distance: always kept.
Remove the most crowded, j at 0.13, then recompute: f goes next.
Then c, k, g and b, one at a time.
Six spread-out members are left, ends included.
scenes.spec: Lecture 15 video, scene 05-prune: lesson 15.2's twelve archive members a..l (L15.P12) pruned to a cap of six by crowding distance (L15.PRUNE): the ends a and l get infinity; remove the smallest distance, recompute, repeat. Removed in order j 0.13, f 0.17, c 0.19, k 0.34, g 0.46, b 0.50; kept a d e h i l. Layout (stage px): L15.plot x 12, y 12, 600 x 616; right panel x 636..924: stats 'archive' (y 12) and 'cap' (y 104), the label 'removed' (y 210) and six grey chips (2 rows of 3, 88 x 70, from y 256) that fill in the removal order. Story (local seconds): 0.3 plot, 0.6 twelve green members; 1.4 the stats (12 and 6); 3.2 a and l ringed with orange '∞' tags (until 5.8); removals at 5.8 / 7.4 / 9.2 / 10.1 / 11.0 / 11.9: ring and orange value tag, +0.4 red cross, +0.6 count drops and the chip fills, +0.6..1.0 the member fades; 12.6 the green line through the six kept; hold to 15.

title: Who should each
particle follow?
caps: Each particle (blue) needs a leader from the archive (green).
Simplest: pick a member at random, each with a 1 in 5 chance.
Or count the particles each member dominates: c dominates four, e one.
Fewer means more likely to lead: e's weight is 1/2, c's only 1/5.
Or use particle P as the reference point: b, c and d dominate it.
Their own boxes: b 1.5, c 4, d 1.5. c covers most, so c leads.
scenes.spec: Lecture 15 video, scene 06-leaders: lesson 15.3's archive a..e (L15.H, green) and swarm particles P..V (L15.SW, blue). Three ways to pick a leader: (1) at random, 1 in 5 each; (2) dominated-solution count: c dominates four particles, e one (L15.COUNT), weight 1 / (1 + count): c 1/5, e 1/2, so e is likelier; (3) hypervolume with particle P (7, 7.5) as the reference point: b, c and d dominate it, their own boxes are 1.5, 4 and 1.5 (L15.HVP, L15.HVBOX), so c leads. Layout (stage px): L15.plot x 12, y 12, 600 x 616; right panel x 636..924: three method cards (y 12 / 172 / 332, h 144), grey until their turn, then orange. Story (local seconds): 0.3 plot, 0.6 archive a..e, 1.2 particles; 3.2 card 1, an orange ring hops a, b, c, d, e, a, b... every 0.2 s and stops on d at 5.0 with a '1 in 5' tag; 6.2 card 2, dashed links from each member to the particles it dominates (6.4..7.4), count tags at 7.4; 9.6 c's and e's tags become '1/5' (grey) and '1/2' (orange); 12.2 card 3, links and tags fade, P ringed, 12.8..13.8 the three boxes grow (green); 14.6 value tags 1.5 / 4 / 1.5, c's box and ring orange; hold to 17.

title: Watch the front
fill out
caps: A real run: ten drone routes (blue) and their archive (green).
Each step the particles follow leaders, and better routes enter the archive.
The archive creeps towards the true front, the dashed line.
Capped at ten, it stays spread along the whole front.
scenes.spec: Lecture 15 video, scene 07-run: a real run of the lessons' drone MOPSO (L15.RUN: 10 particles, archive cap 10, crowding prune, random leader, keep-newest pbest, seed 4), 21 snapshots, iteration 0..20. Particles (blue) glide from one snapshot to the next; the archive (green) is shown snapshot by snapshot; the true front is the dashed grey line (L15.TRUE). Energy above 12 is clipped to the top edge. The archive starts with 5 members and holds 10 (the cap) at the end. Layout (stage px): L15.plot x 12, y 12, 600 x 616, time 0..10, energy 0..12; right panel x 636..924: stats 'iteration' (y 12) and 'archive' (y 104), then legend tags 'swarm' (blue), 'archive' (green), 'true front' (grey) at y 230 / 300 / 370. Story (local seconds): 0.3 plot, 0.5 the dashed true front, 0.8 swarm and archive at iteration 0, stats and legend; iterations step every 0.45 s from 1.4 (iteration 20 at 10.4); 10.6 the archive line draws; hold to 13.

title: When almost
nothing dominates
caps: Around a point, a quarter of space is better on both goals, a quarter worse.
The other half is neither: those points cannot be compared.
Each extra goal halves the share you can compare: 1/32 with six.
So almost every pair is non-dominated, and dominance stops ranking.
scenes.spec: Lecture 15 video, scene 08-many: lesson 15.3's many-objective trouble. Around one point (blue), with two objectives (both minimised) a quarter of the space is better on both (green, it dominates the point), a quarter worse on both (red), and the other half is neither (grey): mutually non-dominating. Only 2 / 2^M of the space is comparable (L15.SHARE): 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/32 for 2, 3, 4 and 6 objectives, so with many objectives almost everything is non-dominated. Layout (stage px): left square 430 x 430 at (24, 60) split into four quadrants with 28 px labels; right: the label 'share you can compare' (x 488..924, y 40) and four bar rows (y 120 + 100 i): '2 goals' etc. (x 488, 130 wide), a grey track 190 wide at x 620 with a green part share x 190, and the fraction (x 828); a solid orange tag at the bottom. Story (local seconds): 0.3 square and point, 0.9 green quadrant, 1.7 red quadrant; 3.4 the two grey quadrants; 6.0 bar rows every 0.8 s (green parts grow 0.5 s); 9.6 the orange tag 'almost everything is non-dominated'; hold to 14.

recap.spec: Lecture 15 · Multi-objective particle swarm optimisation, scene 09-recap: three rows, each a small animated pictogram and one bold line (bare scene). Story (local seconds): 0.1 title and Sprout, rows slide in at 0.8 / 1.9 / 3.0, each pictogram starts 0.4 s after its row, 5.6-6.2 the call to action. EVERY PICTOGRAM PLAYS ONCE AND HOLDS ITS FINISHED FRAME (no loop, no reset): all are done by 6.5 s, so for the last 2.5 seconds only Sprout's bob moves. Row 1 (green): the archive. Three green members on a front; a blue newcomer pops in, the member it dominates turns red with a cross and fades, the newcomer turns green. Row 2 (orange): pruning. Six green members; the two ends get orange rings, the most crowded one turns red, gets a cross and fades. Row 3 (blue): leaders. Four green members and a blue particle; an orange arrow grows from the particle to one member, which gets an orange ring.

helpers: Lecture 15 · Multi-objective particle swarm optimisation: pure data and algorithms (VID.l15, short name L15). NO DOM here. The app's own kernel (js/content/nic/l15-01.js archAdd / pruneCrowd / hv / contrib, l15-02.js the drone MOPSO, l13-01.js dom / crowd / mulberry) is ported line for line, run ONCE when the page loads, and every number the storyboard (videos/_plan/lecture-15.json) quotes is ASSERTED: a wrong figure throws a clear Error. Scenes only look values up. Both objectives are minimised everywhere (time across, energy up; lower is better). KERNEL L15.dom(a, b) a dominates b; L15.archAdd(A, y) -> {A, log ("rm" | "beats" | "tie" per member), added} L15.crowd(P, idx) -> {i: distance}; L15.pruneCrowd(P, cap) -> {keep, out: [[index, distance], ...]} L15.hv(P, r), L15.contrib(P, r) (each member's own share of the hypervolume with reference r) L15.boxes(P, r) -> [{i, a: [x, y], b: [x, y]}] each member's own (exclusive) hypervolume box, sorted by x DATA L15.SWARM9 {ids, P, at}: lesson 15.1's nine routes A..I; L15.FRONT9 = A B C E G (non-dominated), F is the particle. L15.MOVES: one particle's four moves from p best (5, 5); L15.PB = [{y, old, neu, mvOld, mvNew}] after each move (keep oldest: (5,5) (5,5) (5,5) (4.5,4); keep newest: (4,6) (4,6) (3.5,5.5) (4.5,4)). L15.ARCH a1..a5 and L15.NEWS = [{y, R, A}] the three newcomers (2, 4) (5, 4.5) (7, 2) added in turn ((2, 4) removes a2 a3; (5, 4.5) is turned away by (2, 4); (7, 2) joins; final size 5). L15.P12 lesson 15.2's twelve members a..l; L15.PRUNE = pruneCrowd to cap 6: out j f c k g b, keep a d e h i l. L15.H archive a..e and L15.SW particles P..V (lesson 15.3); L15.COUNT[i] = particles member i dominates (a 1, b 1, c 4, d 2, e 1); L15.HVP = contributions with particle P (7, 7.5) as reference: b 1.5, c 4, d 1.5. L15.RUN: 21 snapshots {P, A} (swarm and archive objective vectors) of the lesson's drone MOPSO, seed 4, cap 10, crowding prune, random leader, keep-newest p best; L15.TRUE = the true front (41 points). L15.SHARE(M) = 2 / 2^M, the share of space around a point that dominance can compare. || Lecture 15 · MOPSO: the few drawing helpers shared by the scenes (VID.l15, short name L15). Everything else is reused from Lecture 13 (the page loads l5/common.js and l13/common*.js): L13.plot, L13.tag, L13.stat, L13.card, L13.label, L13.arrow, L13.mark, L13.seq (see their header comments). All calls are pure. COLOUR ROLES of THIS video (videos/_plan/lecture-15.json): green = archive / non-dominated / kept; red = dominated / removed / turned away; blue = the particle, the new position or newcomer looked at; purple = the 'keep oldest' pbest rule; orange = the 'keep newest' rule and attention (infinity, the chosen leader, crowding values); grey = neutral. L15.fmt([x, y]) -> "(4.5, 4)" L15.plot(stage, o) -> L13.plot preset: x 12, y 12, 600 x 616, axes 0..10 (both minimised), xl "time", yl "energy"; any L13.plot option in o overrides (dots, lines, boxes, links counts too). L15.inset(a, b, da, db) -> [a', b']: the segment a..b (px pairs) pulled in by da at a and db at b (for arrows between dots) L15.card(parent, o) -> L13.card that keeps newline (backslash n) line breaks (same set API) L15.step(t, t0, dt, n) -> integer 0..n: which item of a timed sequence is showing (t0 + i * dt starts item i) || Reused: l13/common.js, common-2.js (tag, stat, card, label, chip, arrow, mark, seq), common-3.js (plot); l5/common.js (svg, tick, tone).
